notes.text: The Mandaic expression "riding on the day" undoubtedly reflects the common Akkadian expression RKB ūmē said of the gods "riding on a storm wind" (see Müller-Kessler, "Aramäische Beschwörungen und astronomische Omina ...", pp. 433-35), but the word iuma was surely always simply understood as "day" within Mandaic. As for the expression using the repeated plural in the KTMW insription, we believe that the commonly agreed upon interpretation of similar expressions in the MT as "yearly" is unwarranted and should be rendered "from time to time" and would so suggest is the best understanding of the KTMW passage as well.

notes.text: The G p.p. is generally used in Syriac for the non-progressive present tense instead of the active ptcp. (but see also s.v. ytyb adj.) In unvocalized Jewish texts, however, forms such as יתיב should probably be taken as the active ptcp. whatever the sense, given that explicit p.p. forms are not found in the best vocalized texts. On the other hand, in LJLA texts the bare יתיב is most often just the simple 3.m.s. perfect. The finite forms regularly govern preps b- and ʕl, but both active and passive G participles are often used simply in construct: u-ma-ia-a-ti-ib-a-a-)-i and those who dwell in it Uruk 13. In targumic texts, this verb can match the BH cognate when the sense is nomadic settlement (as at Gen. 20:1), though that is probably no longer a true Aramaic usage.

notes.text: In Eastern Aramaic only in archaic and dialectal contexts, when quoting scripture, or with certain verbs, such as šyn "to pacify", where the semantic context borders on that of the derived nominal yt. Even in reference to Genesis some of the Syriac commentators took the usage to hint at the nominal form (for which see BHCandBak [75]1f.) In some LJLA texts, it is also found with the subject of some verbs (our mng. 4) in a manner somewhat different from the similar occasional BH usage of את, the derived nominal, or the pronominal usage. We take this practice to be ungrammatical due to scribal/authorial uncertainty as to the rection of the verbs in question. One needs also to recognize the grammaticalization of this form as an infix before pronominal suffixes on verbs, especially in later western Aramaic dialects and (perhaps erroneously?) in JBA texts.
